newsitem.title: GERMANY: Euro will stabilise forex markets - French minister.
newsitem.headline: Euro will stabilise forex markets - French minister.

text.p: France's Labour and Social Affairs Minister Jacques Barrot said on Thursday that the status of the planned European Union single currency as a reserve currency would help to counter competitive devaluations from countries including the United States.
Barrot also said he opposed any attempt to let political considerations determine the value of the "euro", and said this was an idea France had well and truly left behind.

"The existence of a stable currency with the European Union behind it will mean this currency can be a reserve currency and therefore create more stability in the international monetary system," Barrot told an invited audience at the conservative Konrad Adenauer Foundation near Bonn.

"What is important is that, if in the future there is a subtle complicity between the U.S. Federal Reserve and the U.S. government, then there will be less scope for such complicity if it comes up against a euro run by an independent central bank."
Barrot insisted that the independent policies of the planned European Central Bank must be aimed only at guaranteeing the stability of the euro, due to be introduced in 1999.
In comments aimed at allaying German fears that the new currency might be weakened by other countries' lax budgetary policies, Barrot told his audience:
"France has understood, admittedly a little late, that it cannot be released from the need for discipline in public finances... by a lax monetary policy."
Asked by a sceptical member of the audience to reaffirm that France no longer saw the level of its currency as a political tool of economic policy, he replied with some irritation:

"Currency and monetary policy belong to an independent institution. That is a given fact. It is a page we have turned. It shouldn't be necessary constantly to keep suggesting that France, at some time in the future, wants to manipulate the euro."
